full_judgment:
47. The writ petitioner filed Affidavit-in-reply on 18.5.2010 against the respondent No.3 and denied the statements and assertion made in affidavit-in-opposition and stated in the preceding Paragraphs that the petitioner could not initiate the construction of the hotel because of the failure by the Government to develop the infrastructural facilities which includes construction of internal roads, water supply, electricity connection and sewerage system in the Hotel Motel zone. It was the reciprocal obligations by the Government to develop the infrastructural facilities consequent upon conclusion of lease deed and delivery of possession thereof upon taking the required consideration money. The Government utterly failed to comply with such reciprocal obligation for which the initiation of the construction work became delayed. So the petitioner cannot be held responsible for the alleged delay and also the same cannot be construed as a breach of the lease deed. Because the Government itself is responsible for the alleged delay. In addition to the above, it is reiterated that the petitioner basically challenged the unlawful cancellation of the settlement of the plots owned by the petitioner. Since while cancelling the settlement of the lease the respondents have not exercised their authority and power in accordance with the law. Rather they have acted out of sheer malice and with the malafide intention to obtain unauthorised gain from such cancellation. In fact, the impugned cancellation notice was issued at the instance of the vested interested quarters without issuing any prior notice and without giving the petitioner any opportunity of being heard. Hence, the respondents have violated the principle of natural justice. The petitioner having had no other alternative and efficacious remedy against such unlawful and arbitrary cancellation by the concerned government authority have filed this Writ Petition before this Hon'ble Court. As such, this Writ Petition is maintainable. Apart from the above, it is also stated in response to the claim of the respondent NO.3 that the petitioner has transferred the leased property to the Power of Attorney holder that such contention is highly misconceived . The Power of Attorney does not readily infer the presumption as to transfer of title. It is merely the authorization of power to do certain specified deeds and things for and on behalf of the principal. The Government can not unilaterally enlarge the scope and authority of the Power of Attorney at its own advantage. 

 (III). PLD 1983 (SC) 344 In the case of contracts for sale of immovable property , the presumption is that time is not of the essence of the contract.
